title: Publish a precise compatibility matrix
trigger: Prospects hesitate because supported devices, operating systems, browsers or input formats are unclear.
action: Provide a concise current compatibility matrix with supported versions and material limitations, linked from the relevant product explanation. Include a simple way to identify the buyer's own setup without requiring a purchase or revealing unnecessary device information.
mechanism: Concrete fit information may resolve a common reason for postponing evaluation.
guardrail: Verify compatibility through actual product support and tests; distinguish unsupported from merely untested environments.
measure: Qualified paid activation; compatibility-related refunds.

title: Explain each sensitive permission request
trigger: The product asks for access that sounds broad, and prospects do not understand why it is needed.
action: Before the permission step, explain what the permission enables, when access occurs and how the user can revoke it. Use the exact permission scope and a representative workflow so the buyer can relate the request to useful behavior.
mechanism: A comprehensible purpose may reduce uncertainty about granting necessary access.
guardrail: Do not minimize access scope or promise restrictions the implementation does not enforce; keep revocation consequences accurate.
measure: Qualified activation after permission; privacy complaints.

title: Map where customer data actually goes
trigger: Trust copy says data is secure but does not explain collection, processing, storage or external providers.
action: Create a plain-language data-flow explanation covering the material stages and applicable retention, with links to current detailed policies. Make distinctions such as local processing versus uploaded processing explicit where they affect the buyer's decision.
mechanism: A concrete model may reduce ambiguity for customers evaluating data risk.
guardrail: Verify actual implementation and approved policies; do not imply legal compliance or confidentiality guarantees without support.
measure: Qualified purchases; data-handling misunderstandings.

title: Demonstrate an available exit path
trigger: Prospects worry they will lose control of useful work if they adopt the product and later leave.
action: Show the existing export formats, deletion process and post-cancellation access rules before commitment, with a small permitted export example where useful. Explain practical limits so portability is a verified capability rather than a vague assurance.
mechanism: Visible reversibility may reduce the perceived cost of making an adoption decision.
guardrail: Do not promise complete portability, immediate deletion or retained access beyond actual behavior and terms.
measure: Qualified paid conversion; exit and data-access complaints.

title: Check import compatibility before commitment
trigger: A buyer has existing data but cannot tell whether the product can accept its structure without a costly migration.
action: Offer a safe schema or sample-file check that reports supported fields, required transformations and known limits before purchase. Distinguish this preflight from importing real records, and provide a clear result the buyer can inspect.
mechanism: Reducing migration uncertainty may help an otherwise suitable buyer move forward.
guardrail: Use appropriate handling for uploaded data; do not guarantee a complete migration from a small sample check.
measure: Qualified migration-related purchases; import failures.

title: Show the migration sequence and ownership
trigger: Migration copy says switching is easy but leaves buyers unsure what they must move and who performs each step.
action: Publish the actual migration sequence, responsibilities and supported transfer methods, including any period when both systems run. Separate included assistance from optional paid services, and explain what information cannot be transferred automatically.
mechanism: A concrete transition plan may reduce fear of disruption and hidden work.
guardrail: Use operationally supported steps; new migration services or guarantees require a commercial decision.
measure: Qualified purchases replacing another tool; migration abandonment.

title: Budget the customer's setup effort
trigger: The page calls setup quick while the buyer must gather files, obtain permissions or configure external services.
action: List the customer's real preparation tasks and the work the product performs, separating required steps from optional customization. Offer measured effort estimates only where suitable evidence exists, and show available documentation beside the difficult dependency.
mechanism: Predictable effort may feel more manageable than an unspecified setup burden.
guardrail: Do not invent completion times or hide approval delays; verify that optional steps are genuinely optional.
measure: Paid activation; setup-related refunds and support.

title: Explain behavior during a service interruption
trigger: Reliability statements do not tell buyers what happens to ongoing work when connectivity or a provider fails.
action: Describe the product's actual interrupted-state behavior: what is preserved, what pauses, what can continue and how recovery is communicated. Show a real status or recovery route so a buyer can judge the operational consequence.
mechanism: Understanding failure consequences may reduce uncertainty more usefully than a broad reliability slogan.
guardrail: Verify the fallback and retention behavior; do not promise offline use, automatic recovery or response times that do not exist.
measure: Qualified paid adoption; interruption-related data loss and complaints.

title: Align service capacity with the sold allowance
trigger: The public offer promises usable capacity while effective service budgets or account caps may stop work sooner.
action: Trace the advertised allowance against actual enforced limits and operating capacity before emphasizing the purchase. Resolve discrepancies through an authorized operational or commercial decision, then describe applicable limits and resets accurately at the decision point.
mechanism: A deliverable offer may protect trust, activation and retained purchases.
guardrail: Do not raise spending limits without authorization or treat a higher quota as funded capacity; verify the effective deployed configuration.
measure: Successful paid usage; blocked-within-allowance events and refunds.

title: Explain what happens at a usage limit
trigger: The allowance is stated, but buyers cannot tell whether reaching it stops work, deletes data or creates extra charges.
action: Describe the exact limit behavior and available next steps using the existing product rules: pause, reset, optional purchase or continued read access as applicable. Distinguish calendar resets from permanent caps and retain visibility of unfinished work.
mechanism: Predictable boundaries may reduce fear of bill shock or losing progress.
guardrail: Do not invent rollover, free overages or guaranteed reset timing; keep actual extra charges and consent requirements explicit.
measure: Qualified paid conversion; quota and unexpected-charge complaints.

title: State the support that is included
trigger: Prospects need help but cannot distinguish documentation access, email assistance and any response commitments.
action: Show the actual support channels, availability and plan-specific scope beside the relevant adoption explanation. State a response target only when it is approved and achievable, and provide a realistic route for questions before buying.
mechanism: Accessible expectations may reduce uncertainty about being left alone with a problem.
guardrail: Do not promise round-the-clock or immediate service from an unstaffed channel; keep paid assistance separate from included support.
measure: Qualified purchases; unmet support expectations and workload.

title: Show how uncertain AI output is handled
trigger: An AI product presents only confident answers while the buyer's task requires checking ambiguity or errors.
action: Explain and demonstrate the actual mechanisms for uncertainty, source inspection, human review or escalation. Make the user's responsibility and the product's known limitations understandable before the buyer relies on a sample result.
mechanism: A realistic verification path may make a useful capability easier to trust appropriately.
guardrail: Do not imply error-free output, expert approval or escalation services that are absent; preserve the intended-use boundaries.
measure: Qualified paid activation; harmful reliance and correction burden.

title: Make recoverable changes easy to understand
trigger: Customers worry that an accidental edit or import will permanently damage their existing work.
action: Explain the product's real undo, version history, backup or restore capability with a concrete supported example and its time or scope limits. Let the buyer understand which actions are reversible before using them.
mechanism: Perceived reversibility may reduce hesitation around adopting a new workflow.
guardrail: Verify restoration behavior and permissions; never generalize a local undo control into a full backup guarantee.
measure: Qualified paid activation; unrecoverable-change incidents.

title: Clarify collaboration permissions before purchase
trigger: A team buyer cannot tell who will see, edit, approve or administer shared work.
action: Provide a concise role-and-permission example for the actual product, including guest or external collaborator boundaries when supported. Link detailed controls for buyers who need them, and map plan restrictions accurately without requiring account setup to learn the basics.
mechanism: Clear control boundaries may reduce collaboration and confidentiality objections.
guardrail: Verify actual permissions and default sharing; do not invent granular access controls or imply every plan includes them.
measure: Qualified team purchases; permission-related support and incidents.

title: Explain ownership of inputs and outputs
trigger: Prospects cannot determine whether the vendor can reuse their material or whether they may use generated outputs.
action: Summarize the applicable approved ownership, license and permitted-use terms in plain language, with a direct link to the governing policy. Separate customer inputs, generated outputs and third-party material where the actual terms differ.
mechanism: Reduced contractual ambiguity may help buyers assess whether the product fits their intended use.
guardrail: Use the real current terms and appropriate review; do not invent ownership rights or give broad legal guarantees.
measure: Qualified paid conversion; rights and reuse objections.

title: Describe verified accessibility support
trigger: A buyer or purchaser for someone else needs to know whether the product works with their access requirements.
action: Publish the tested interaction capabilities relevant to the workflow, such as keyboard operation, zoom or screen-reader support, with known limitations and a contact route. Give specific findings rather than an unqualified accessibility badge.
mechanism: Concrete compatibility may help a buyer judge usability for their actual needs.
guardrail: Distinguish tested features from full conformance; do not claim certification or universal accessibility without evidence.
measure: Qualified accessible-use activation; blocked-task reports.

title: Disclose required external subscriptions early
trigger: The offer appears self-contained, but useful operation requires a paid third-party account, license or service.
action: Identify each essential external dependency near the related use case and explain which account level or permission is required. Separate optional enhancements from prerequisites so the buyer can assess the complete setup before purchasing.
mechanism: Early dependency clarity may prevent uncertainty and unexpected adoption costs.
guardrail: Verify current dependency requirements and avoid implying that third-party fees are included unless they are.
measure: Qualified paid activation; dependency-related refunds.

title: Explain compatibility through product updates
trigger: Buyers worry that an integration or customized workflow will break as the service evolves.
action: Describe the existing approach to version support, deprecation notices and migration assistance, linking current policy or documentation. Make the supported stability boundary clear instead of promising that every integration will work unchanged forever.
mechanism: Predictability may reduce the perceived long-term cost of adopting a connected tool.
guardrail: Use approved actual practices; new support periods or contractual guarantees are commercial changes.
measure: Qualified long-term purchases; update-related churn and support.

title: Clarify buying for another person
trigger: A relative, administrator or sponsor wants to pay while a different person will use the product.
action: Explain the supported relationship between payer, account owner and user, including setup permissions and who can access billing or product data. Provide the correct existing route without implying shared access that the terms or implementation do not allow.
mechanism: Removing ownership ambiguity may help a willing purchaser complete an appropriate purchase.
guardrail: Verify account and payment rules; do not create accounts, expose another person's data or send invitations without authorization.
measure: Appropriate sponsored purchases; ownership and access disputes.

title: Make incident communication concrete
trigger: A prospect asks how they would learn about a problem affecting their data or service, but the page offers only generic reassurance.
action: Point to the actual incident communication channels and explain the applicable notification process in approved terms. Identify what customers can check themselves and how to reach support, keeping guarantees separate from ordinary operating practice.
mechanism: A concrete response process may reduce uncertainty about the consequences of a future problem.
guardrail: Do not promise legal notice periods, personal contact or response guarantees without a supported policy; never conceal an active material incident.
measure: Qualified paid adoption; incident-communication complaints.
